headline: Fuel prices jump by Tk20 per litre for four types of fuel
summary: Diesel, kerosene, petrol, and octane prices have increased by Tk20 per litre starting Monday, as the government seeks to reduce BPC losses.
details: Fuel prices in Bangladesh have increased by Tk20 per litre for diesel, kerosene, petrol, and octane. The new prices, effective from Monday (September 21), are Tk135 for diesel, Tk155 for kerosene, Tk160 for petrol, and Tk165 for octane.

The Energy and Mineral Resources Division issued a notification on Sunday (September 20) announcing the hike. Previously, diesel was Tk115, kerosene was Tk135, petrol was Tk140, and octane was Tk145 per litre.
According to the notification, fuel prices and freight charges in the international market have risen significantly since March due to ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.

The government stated that prices were not fully adjusted in the domestic market for public interest, leading to a loss of approximately Tk22,875.66 crore for the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) between March and August.

The BPC is currently facing a loss of about Tk89 per litre on diesel, resulting in a daily loss of approximately Tk109 crore. Without adjustment, annual losses on diesel alone could reach Tk40,000 crore.
By increasing the price by Tk20 per litre, the government expects to reduce BPC's annual losses by approximately Tk10,000 crore.
caption:

The Energy and Mineral Resources Division issued a notification on Sunday (September 20) announcing the hike. Previously, diesel was Tk115, kerosene was Tk135, petrol was Tk140, and octane was Tk145 per litre.

According to the notification, fuel prices and freight charges in the international market have risen significantly since March due to ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.

The government stated that prices were not fully adjusted in the domestic market for public interest, leading to a loss of approximately Tk22,875.66 crore for the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) between March and August.

The BPC is currently facing a loss of about Tk89 per litre on diesel, resulting in a daily loss of approximately Tk109 crore. Without adjustment, annual losses on diesel alone could reach Tk40,000 crore.

By increasing the price by Tk20 per litre, the government expects to reduce BPC's annual losses by approximately Tk10,000 crore.

headline: MP Gazi Nazrul and first wife detained after second wife's body found
summary: Police took the Satkhira-4 MP and his first wife into custody for questioning after the body of his 19-year-old second wife was found hanging in a Dhaka flat.
details: Police have taken Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul and his first wife, Maksuda Khanam, into custody for questioning at the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station.
The action follows the discovery of the body of the MP's second wife, 19-year-old Mariyam Khatun, who was found hanging from the ceiling of a flat in the NAM building on Manik Mia Avenue in Dhaka.
Deputy Commissioner Ibn Mizan of the DMP's Tejgaon Division confirmed the detention, stating that both are being held for investigation purposes.
The incident has resurfaced discussions regarding the MP's personal life; in July, private videos of Gazi Nazrul and Mariyam Khatun had circulated on social media.
Following the controversy surrounding those videos, Jamaat-e-Islami expelled the lawmaker from the party on July 22.
Police are continuing their investigation to determine the exact circumstances surrounding the death of the 19-year-old.
caption:
A lawmaker and his first wife are in police custody after the body of his 19-year-old second wife was found hanging in a Dhaka flat.

Police have taken Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul and his first wife, Maksuda Khanam, into custody for questioning at the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station.

The action follows the discovery of the body of the MP's second wife, 19-year-old Mariyam Khatun, who was found hanging from the ceiling of a flat in the NAM building on Manik Mia Avenue in Dhaka.

Deputy Commissioner Ibn Mizan of the DMP's Tejgaon Division confirmed the detention, stating that both are being held for investigation purposes.

The incident has resurfaced discussions regarding the MP's personal life; in July, private videos of Gazi Nazrul and Mariyam Khatun had circulated on social media.

Following the controversy surrounding those videos, Jamaat-e-Islami expelled the lawmaker from the party on July 22.

Police are continuing their investigation to determine the exact circumstances surrounding the death of the 19-year-old.
